title: Connecting to a local server and to a remote one

videos.script: Every server so far ran on ana's machine, as ana, started by her host. This lesson moves one to a second machine and asks what changes. {{title}} The second machine is a network namespace with its own address, a certificate from the lab's own authority, and a user of its own. ana cannot read its files, and it cannot read hers. {{machine}} Asked without a token, the server answers four hundred and one, and points at a metadata document that names its authorization server. A client can follow that chain without being told anything in advance. {{discovery}} Four tokens, four outcomes: one that may read, one that may also refund, one issued for a different server, and one that has expired. {{tokens}} And what the lab leaves out on purpose. The authorization server here publishes its metadata and issues nothing, so the lesson says how the full OAuth flow goes instead of pretending to run it. {{last}}
